definitions.explanation: A friend or close acquaintance. More literary or formal than {友達|ともだち}. Often used in compound words or literary contexts.

examples.japanese: {友|とも}あり{遠方|えんぽう}より{来|き}たる。
examples.notes: Famous quote from the Analects of Confucius

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{苦楽|くらく}を{共|とも}にした{友|とも}だ。
examples.english: He is a friend who has shared both hardships and joys with me.

examples.japanese: {旧友|きゅうゆう}は{良|よ}き{友|とも}だ。
examples.english: An old friend is a good friend.

examples.japanese: {困|こま}った{時|とき}の{友|とも}こそ{真|しん}の{友|とも}だ。
examples.english: A friend in need is a friend indeed.

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい}の{友|とも}と{久|ひさ}しぶりに{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I met up with a friend from my school days after a long time.

notes:
USAGE: {友|とも} is more literary and formal than {友達|ともだち}. It appears frequently in compounds, proverbs, and classical expressions.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{友人|ゆうじん} (friend - formal)
・{友情|ゆうじょう} (friendship)
・{親友|しんゆう} (close friend)
・{旧友|きゅうゆう} (old friend)
・{学友|がくゆう} (school friend)
・{戦友|せんゆう} (comrade in arms)
・{友好|ゆうこう} (friendship, amity)

CLASSICAL EXPRESSIONS:
・{友|とも}あり{遠方|えんぽう}より{来|き}たる (A friend comes from afar - Confucius)
・{良|よ}き{友|とも} (a good friend)

CONTRAST:
・{友|とも} - literary/formal
・{友達|ともだち} - everyday word for friend
